answer: Unchecked agent congestion can spiral the system into gridlock if synthetic traffic enters without friction. The network reaches a nadir when fake identities saturate critical capacity nodes, overwhelming routing logic. To choke this flow, ingress tolls require agents to stake proof-of-work resources, matching the high computational burn of a physical gale to force real economic costs on every minted route. Attackers face unsustainable thermodynamic expenses to flood lanes, yet static tolls risk bypassing adaptable routing loops if edge demand shifts dynamically.
